_comment: The next-release lane as a graph the JEV graph guard judges. The strategic decision - which node lands FIRST - is made by JEV from the evidence, not asserted by the seat. Run: python harness/harness2/compositor.py --mode graph --input harness/next-release/graph.json --wave next-release
_evidence: docs/intake/next-release-intake-2026-11-06.md (adjudicated 2026-11-06) and docs/intake/src/synapse_next_release_blueprint.md (SHA-256 167ca678f620e6a0) Revised 2026-11-07: RULING-2026-11-07-round2.md (R1-R4) adds NR-SPARSE-RENDER, two owner-file extensions and behavioural predicates.
objective: Deliver one trustworthy loop: prove which render products this attempt produced, report authored writes truthfully through every installed route, and qualify one useful OpenCV 5.1 CUDA vision chain on the RTX 4090 behind a supervised worker, with durable evidence. Land the evidence and the contract fixes first, then the GPU feasibility, then the integrated slice; qualify the final artifact pair last.
standards: Law 1: every check must be able to fail. A check that cannot fail is deleted rather than kept green.
Law 2: no number without a producer path. Every figure names the command or probe that produces it.
Law 3: status describes what happened, not what was intended.
Probe truth beats pinned constants: where the live build disagrees with a document, the live build wins.
One owner per file. Two nodes that claim the same file are serialized by plain code; a conflict is a finding, not a race.
Absence of a symbol from a table is not proof of absence. The decisive test is calling it on an instance.
No hardcoded user paths. Every probe and the installer must work on a clean machine.
A GPU flag, device count or utilisation percentage is not a CUDA-success receipt. The executed dispatch branch is.
A result file is not success; a committed terminal receipt is. An orphan after a crash is evidence, not a pass.

nodes.title: Make the live render path honour an explicit frame list
nodes.why: NR-PLAN-TRUTH grades the artist's sparse set in the driver, but the shipped handler reads only start_frame/end_frame/step, render_farm builds a contiguous range, and the MCP schema exposes no frames, so a sparse request still renders the invented frame. The seam crosses an ownership boundary (HANDS render handlers vs CONDUCTOR autonomy), so it is its own node rather than an extension.

nodes.title: Make the original render plan immutable and reconcile sparse, missing and unsupported shapes
nodes.why: G101 and G32 prove per-attempt product truth; neither keeps the original plan immutable nor computes retry targets from it. Sparse [1,3] with a retry [3], a missing terminal product with no evaluation row, and a multi-render-step plan that is silently truncated to the first step are all still reachable. The blueprint's adversarial cases in section 12.2 are the fixtures. Round-two ruling R2: models.py joins the node because the report must carry executed state; the predicate is behavioural (R4) after the attack proved the grep could not fail. Round 2.5 (R2b): handlers.py stays with NR-WRITE-RECEIPT; plan-truth does not write it.

nodes.title: Give authored writes a receipt that survives success, failure and every installed route
nodes.why: G25 returns observed, mismatch and a refusal, but a lost transport loses the detail, an uninspectable parm can read as no animation, and queued mutations carry no precondition. The blueprint's section 6 receipt (request, write, readback, recovery, error) and the raw-authored comparison domain are the contract; the legacy observed value stays evaluated. Round-two ruling R3: the contract is every installed route, so the rewrap, stdio server and panel executor join the node; the predicate is behavioural (R4). Round 2.5 (R3b): the panel consumers that stringify the exception join the node, because a receipt the consumer drops did not survive the route. R2b: the _record_autonomy_task repoint lands here, with a getattr fallback.

nodes.title: Prove one useful OpenCV 5.1 CUDA chain on the RTX 4090 and freeze its build
nodes.why: Nothing in the repo establishes a working OpenCV 5.1 CUDA build on Windows. The official wheels are CPU-only. This node answers the only question that can stop the release: does the named chain execute, with which exact commits, toolchain, module flags and CUDA runtime, and what does it cost. It is a probe plus a build lock, not a product change.

nodes.title: Qualify the GPU chain against analytic fixtures and an independent CPU reference
nodes.why: Source support, a built module, an executed call and a release-qualified operation are four different states. Owner ruling 2026-11-07: the first GPU chain to qualify is the change-mask body in retina/t1.py - absdiff, threshold, morphological open and close (R2) - on the artifact built under E:/OpenCV5.1_Prep (R3), not C:/ocv. Owner rulings 2026-11-08: the change-mask chain is qualified beside the masked meanStdDev census, which stays a later closure item with its hand-computable fixtures (neutral RGB ramps, the 11x11 census, signed HDR, NaN/Inf counts, equality at the FP32 threshold) - ADR-0002 decision 14 option (ii) (OD-22); the cpu_reference is the stock opencv-python-headless 5.0.0.93 wheel in its own venv (OD-10); and this node's gate is joe (OD-23). G0-proposed, not ruled (G0 receipt slice 2; report 02-ops section 7): the change-mask fixtures (changes at frame edges and corners; |diff| at and one float32 ulp either side of diff_threshold; non-contiguous and odd-stride arrays; sizes not multiples of 16 or 32; an empty change set) and identical mask bytes as the parity criterion. INFERENCE: a NaN in a luma plane is a CPU-versus-CUDA threshold-parity hazard, so the draft predicate also asks for a NaN fixture. The backend witness and a per-operation dispatch record still turn the second state into the fourth.

nodes.title: Freeze one image and evidence contract: named RGB, derived Y, invalid-sample policy
nodes.why: T1 averages channels and the beauty ingest defaults to a subimage, so alpha and data channels can enter luminance. The Y coefficients must come from the declared RGB-to-XYZ transform, not from Rec.709 weights applied to ACEScg. Source-invalid pixels must block dependent statistics with exact counts rather than being dropped or zeroed.

nodes.title: Run the vision chain in a supervised worker through one thin host adapter
nodes.why: RETINA has modules and a designed process boundary, not a deployed executable path. The worker must own its cv2/OIIO/CUDA binaries outside Houdini's DLL search path, take allowlisted operations and read-only roots, and run off the main thread. This is also the first place the evidence envelope crosses a process boundary. Owner ruling 2026-11-07 (R4): the worker runtime is CPython 3.12.10 with the isolated cp312 OpenImageIO wheel, not a hython-seeded venv and not the cp314 wheel.

nodes.title: Publish results durably: one terminal receipt, restart-rebuildable, late replies never win
nodes.why: Without a terminal selection receipt, a result file after a crash, a lost acknowledgement or a superseded request can all read as success. The repo already has the atomic publication pattern in loop/coordinator.py; this node applies it to RETINA requests and results, including cancellation ordering and orphan quarantine.

nodes.title: Ship an independently versioned worker artifact and qualify the host/worker pair and rollback
nodes.why: The payload builder ships an allowlist; adding worker sources does not ship them. The release needs a worker build lock, a host/worker compatibility handshake, and a tested data-preserving rollback. Current Setup refuses ordinary downgrades and refuses maintenance while Houdini runs, so rollback is a procedure to qualify, not a flag to flip.

nodes.title: Make the third-party notice set, CUDA EULA compliance and Qt relinkability a release gate
nodes.why: SYNAPSE is MIT and OpenCV/contrib are Apache-2.0, so nothing blocks commercial use. The obligations are concrete: Apache/BSD notices, the NVIDIA Attachment A binaries and EULA text, OPENCV_ENABLE_NONFREE=OFF in the build lock, and the pre-existing PySide6 LGPLv3 relinkability duty. A release that misses them is a legal defect, not a documentation one.

nodes.title: Curated memory handoff and the isolated SL0 pilot, after the core release
nodes.why: The blueprint keeps these explicitly out of the release. They are listed so the graph does not silently drop them, and parked so plain code does not schedule them.
nodes.parked: Follow-on. Neither blocks the core release.

nodes.title: Build the OpenCV 5.1 CUDA artifact under the ruled E: root and lock its identity
nodes.why: No graph node owns the build (G0 receipt section 13 item 2; ADR-0002 decision 13). NR-GPU-FEASIBILITY closed B1 with a trivial non-OpenCV kernel and its predicate pins feasible-unproven, so it would go red exactly when a build succeeds (inverse gate). Under R3 the build runs under E:/OpenCV5.1_Prep, whose staged BUILD_LIST names cudaarithm and cudafilters for the R2 change-mask chain, and under R4 the binding targets CPython 3.12.10 without the limited API. The staged recipe has no install step. The receipt must record the generated (not requested) module list, both pinned source SHAs, the install step, where cv2 landed, native-file digests, OPENCV_ENABLE_NONFREE=OFF and measured durations. OD-02 was settled on 2026-11-08 by Joe's merge of this node: it owns the build (ADR-0002 decision 13, option b). Still waits on OD-12 (build authorization, window, parallelism) and OD-16 (worker venv).

nodes.title: Pin the host/worker boundary: transitive zero-cv2 in-host closure, zero hou in the worker, fixed host payload
nodes.why: The zero-cv2 host lint is lexical, not transitive, no test pins zero hou in the worker, and the host installer already ships retina/t1.py, so a backend module could load CUDA into Houdini with every test green (ADR-0002 Context section 2 items 5-7). These are G0 slice 1 (G0 receipt section 11): three hermetic tests, each proven able to fail by a named mutation. ADR-0002 was ratified on 2026-11-08 (OD-11), so they are a precondition for any backend code under retina/ (ADR-0002 section 'Consequences', item 4). OD-09 was settled on 2026-11-08 by Joe's merge of this node: it owns the guard tests (ADR-0002 decision 12, option a). Still waits on OD-05 (the build_payload.py allowlist coupling).

nodes.title: Make the RETINA worker runtime recipe conform to R4: CPython 3.12.10, isolated cp312 OIIO, the locked custom cv2
nodes.why: The shipped recipe documents a hython-seeded venv and names a cp314 OpenImageIO wheel, which R4 rules out, and it installs opencv-python-headless, which must never share a venv with the custom cv2 (ADR-0002 section 'Consequences of R1-R4', item 3). The three recipe files are in no node's owner_files, so they cannot change until a node owns them (G0 receipt section 5). The contract names CPython 3.12.10, the cp312 win_amd64 OIIO wheel, NumPy inside >=2,<3 and compatible with the build headers, and the build-lock receipt by digest. OD-09 was settled on 2026-11-08 by Joe's merge of this node: it owns the three recipe files (ADR-0002 decision 12, option a). Still waits on OD-16 (worker venv location and creator; CUDA DLL resolution).

nodes.title: Add the worker-only CUDA backend for the R2 change-mask chain behind the tri-state contract
nodes.why: ADR-0002 Site 2 is a worker-only CUDA module, off the host payload list and unreachable from the in-host modules, and it is unowned. Under R2 it covers absdiff, the strict threshold, morphological open and close only. A gpu_required operation that cannot run on CUDA must yield an inconclusive check with a reason, never a silent CPU pass, and T1Unavailable must be mapped rather than raised. No backend code may land under retina/ before ADR-0002 is ratified (G0 receipt section 13 item 22). Ruled 2026-11-08: Joe ratified ADR-0002 (OD-11); his merge of this node settled its graph home (OD-09; ADR-0002 decision 12, option a); the cpu_reference is the stock opencv-python-headless 5.0.0.93 wheel in its own venv (OD-10).

nodes.title: Run the GPU-required profile as Joe's canary on approved non-production scenes, with disable and rollback shown
nodes.why: The OpenCV blueprint's G4 has no node (ADR-0002 Reconciliation, G4 row). It comes after demo v1 and needs a specific approval, a re-grounded runtime, render, cancel and contention probes, and an immediate disable and rollback shown with before and after evidence. Worker-package rollback is unavailable until NR-WORKER-SUPERVISED and NR-PACKAGE-PAIR exist. Waits on OD-12 (what demo v1 means; resource window) and OD-21 (canary before or after packaging). Joe's merge of 2026-11-08 keeps it parked behind the worker.

edges.why: there is nothing to qualify until a build and a chain exist
the contract must name operations the qualified build actually dispatches
the worker implements a contract; it does not invent one
a worker that cannot prove its backend has nothing to ship
publication rules are meaningful only once a worker writes results
the pair is qualified against committed receipts, not against ad-hoc files
the product key and attempt identity the envelope carries come from the plan
vision proposals may only mutate through the authored-write receipt path
no artifact pair ships without its notices and EULA compliance
follow-ons start after the release, not beside it
the plan's sparse set is only meaningful once the live path renders exactly those frames
B1 (nvcc 13.3 accepts MSVC 19.44) is the build's input; the build does not re-litigate it
OPENCV_ENABLE_NONFREE=OFF belongs in the build lock
R3: the qualification artifact is the one built under E:/OpenCV5.1_Prep; nothing else qualifies
the worker recipe names the locked artifact by digest
the worker lock must cite the build-lock artifact identity, not re-derive it
R4: the supervised worker runs the recipe this node makes conform
the retina/t1.py seam must keep the in-host closure free of any backend
zero hou in the worker and zero cv2 in the host hold across the process boundary
the guards are a precondition for any backend code under retina/ (ADR-0002 section 'Consequences', item 4)
a backend may only dispatch operations the qualified artifact proved
the backend plugs into the cpu_reference seam that node owns in retina/t1.py
the backend runs only in the R4 worker runtime
the worker loads the backend only when the mode is gpu_required; off and cpu load nothing new
a canary needs a launched, supervised worker
canary results are committed terminal receipts, not result files
the canary exercises the backend in gpu_required mode
a canary verdict gains no mutation authority; any proposal mutates only through the authored-write receipt path
if Joe orders canary before packaging (OD-21), the pair qualification cites the canary receipt

seams.seam: the render plan is the only source of what was asked for
seams.blast_radius: every retry, every coverage denominator, every 'missing' claim

seams.seam: the evidence envelope crosses the process boundary
seams.blast_radius: T0/T1 verdicts, the worker result, the panel readout

seams.seam: the worker owns native binaries outside Houdini's search path
seams.blast_radius: the DCC's image I/O, every render, the panel's import graph

seams.seam: the installer allowlist decides what ships
seams.blast_radius: the worker exists in development and is absent in the release

seams.seam: the GPU profile is persisted state
seams.blast_radius: a silent CPU fallback can satisfy nothing while reporting success
